claim: projectile TTLs were left as bare 4TPS tick counts, so the 20TPS cutover shortened them fivefold; they now derive from vanilla game-tick values and keep their original real time
what_happened: the cutover commit reported that TTLs kept their real time. They did not: ttl 240 was 60s at 250ms per tick and 12s at 50ms per tick. An arrow lived 12s instead of 60s, a pearl 2.5s instead of 12.5s.
fix: arrow 1200 game ticks (60s), mob arrow 800 (40s), pearl 250 (12.5s), snowball 300 (15s), each converted with server_ticks. This restores pre-cutover behaviour; it is not a vanilla-faithful removal.
not_done: vanilla has no flying TTL and 1200 counts ticks in the ground, so removing the TTL would change results and risk entity accumulation. Deferred to its own slice.
how_found: the recorded search pattern ttl: [0-9]+ across src/main.rs. This is the third literal of this class, after lava t % 2 and air 60.
lesson: a conversion declared as real-time preserving must be verified by search, not by declaration. Declaring it is not implementing it.
tests: 35 passed, 0 failed, 1 explicitly ignored, serial and at 8 threads
negative_control: ARROW_TTL_GT set back to 240: the test fails with arrow no longer spans 60000ms, left 12000
review: NOT RUN, external usage limit still in force
